company.name: Ledgerly
company.description: Invoicing and payments for freelancers and small businesses: send an invoice, get paid by transfer, keep the books tidy.

title: Ledgerly: your first sprint as PM
brief: You joined Ledgerly on Monday. The previous PM left a backlog that mixes customer bugs, promises from sales and ideas from the founder, and nobody has ranked it. Growth has slowed because new signups do not finish setting up. Plan the next two-week sprint: the team can only deliver part of this list.

hidden.keyInsight: Of the 22 tickets, 4 are traps and 1 critical problem is filed as minor. Mid-sprint, a production incident forces a replan: the plan that wins keeps room to react.
hidden.principle: Loud is not the same as important. Weigh a request by how many customers it helps and what happens if you wait, not by who asked or how often.

stakeholders.name: Daniel
priorities: Hit the growth number promised to the board
Have something impressive to show investors

stakeholders.name: Laura
priorities: Close the deals in this quarter's pipeline
Never tell a prospect 'it is not on the roadmap'

stakeholders.name: Aisha
priorities: Fix what customers complain about every day

stakeholders.name: Luca
priorities: Time to pay down tech debt

stakeholders.name: Sofia
priorities: More signups from the same traffic
A launch to talk about every month

stakeholders.name: Tomás
priorities: Customer money and data handled by the book

tickets.title: SAML single sign-on for larger accounts
tickets.description: Security teams at larger prospects will not approve a tool without SSO. Sales has been answering 'soon' for two quarters.

visible.impactHint: Required in 6 open deals; 3 were lost over it last quarter.

hidden.explanation: The same requirement across many deals is the market talking, not one customer. Expensive, but it unlocks a whole segment.

tickets.title: Home screen takes 6 to 9 seconds to load for large accounts
tickets.description: The home query loads every record before paginating. The accounts with the most data, which are also the ones that pay the most, get the slowest product.

visible.impactHint: p95 load time is 8.4s for the top 10% of accounts.

hidden.explanation: Performance pain concentrated in the highest-value accounts, backed by measurements. It protects retention where it matters most.

tickets.title: Replace 'Something went wrong' with actionable errors
tickets.description: Every failure shows the same generic message. Users cannot tell whether to retry, fix their input or contact us.

hidden.explanation: Reduces confusion and some tickets, but it spreads thin across many small cases.

tickets.title: Occasional duplicate records after saving
tickets.description: A few users on slow connections see the same record twice after clicking Save. Deleting one of the copies sometimes removes both.

hidden.explanation: 'Sometimes removes both' is silent data loss. The low ticket count hides a bug that destroys customer data, and it will grow with usage.

tickets.title: Remove the legacy v1 API code
tickets.description: No client has called v1 since March, but its code paths still have to be kept compiling and tested.

hidden.explanation: Tidy and safe to do, but nothing gets worse if it waits another sprint.

tickets.title: Board dashboard with weekly KPIs
tickets.description: The CEO assembles the board numbers by hand from three tools every month. A dashboard would give them live.

hidden.explanation: Saves one person a couple of hours a month. Real but small, and no customer ever sees it.

tickets.title: Let users choose which emails they receive
tickets.description: Today it is all or nothing. Users who find one notification noisy unsubscribe from everything, including the emails that bring them back.

hidden.explanation: Protects the re-engagement channel, but the effect is indirect and gradual. Worth doing when there is room.

tickets.title: Alerting on error rates and queue depth
tickets.description: Today the team learns about incidents from customer emails. Basic alerts would cut detection time from hours to minutes.

visible.impactHint: Last incident went unnoticed for 3 hours.

hidden.explanation: Every future incident gets shorter. High leverage for a few points.

tickets.title: Animated 3D hero on the marketing homepage
tickets.description: An interactive 3D scene at the top of the homepage, like the ones the big brands have. It would make us look like a category leader.

hidden.explanation: High reach, zero evidence it changes signups, and it slows the page that converts visitors.

tickets.title: Hold and send balances in EUR and GBP
tickets.description: Customers with European suppliers convert through their bank and lose on the rate. They ask whether we will support other currencies.

visible.impactHint: Asked for by 14 accounts this quarter.

hidden.explanation: Real demand from several accounts, but it needs new banking partners and licences. Too big to justify against cheaper wins this sprint.

tickets.title: Login loop on Safari since last Tuesday's release
tickets.description: Safari users are sent back to the login page after entering correct credentials. There is no workaround except switching browser.

hidden.explanation: A large group of users is locked out of the product by a regression. That is an incident, not a backlog item.

tickets.title: Navigation is unusable on narrow screens
tickets.description: On the smallest phones the open menu sits on top of the page and hides the main button. Found during the last design review.

hidden.explanation: Same work as LED-417 ("Main menu covers the content on small phones"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Authenticator app as a second factor
tickets.description: Login codes go by SMS only. They fail when customers travel and they are the weakest option against account takeover.

visible.impactHint: SMS codes fail for 6% of logins from abroad.

hidden.explanation: Improves both security and reliability of login. Good value at a moderate cost.

tickets.title: Resume identity verification where the user left off
tickets.description: Verification restarts from step one if the user closes the window. Most people do not have their documents at hand the first time.

visible.impactHint: 41% of applicants abandon at the document photo step.

hidden.explanation: Verification is the gate every new customer must pass, and four in ten are lost there. Measured, universal and moderate in cost.

tickets.title: Automate the daily ledger reconciliation
tickets.description: Finance operations compare our ledger with the bank file by hand every morning. Mismatches are found a day late.

visible.impactHint: Two hours of manual work every morning.

hidden.explanation: Finds money discrepancies the same day and frees two hours daily. It is infrastructure the business stands on.

tickets.title: Activity log for account admins
tickets.description: Admins want to see who changed what and when. Security questionnaires from larger prospects ask for it explicitly.

hidden.explanation: A genuine requirement for larger accounts, but it only matters to a slice of the pipeline and it is not small.

tickets.title: On-premise installation for Vantage Motors
tickets.description: Vantage Motors's IT policy does not allow cloud tools. They would sign this quarter if we give them a version to run in their own data centre.

visible.impactHint: Would be our biggest contract ever.

hidden.explanation: A second product to build, ship and support forever, for one logo. The contract size hides the permanent cost.

tickets.title: Fix contrast and keyboard focus on the core flows
tickets.description: Fourteen screens fail WCAG AA contrast and the main form cannot be completed with a keyboard.

hidden.explanation: The right thing to do and a growing requirement in procurement, but no deadline is attached yet.

tickets.title: Add indexes for the five slowest queries
tickets.description: Five queries account for most of the database load. All of them scan full tables.

visible.impactHint: p95 latency doubles at peak hours.

hidden.explanation: A small, well-understood change that every user feels at peak time.

tickets.title: Main menu covers the content on small phones
tickets.description: On screens narrower than 360px the menu stays open over the page. Users have to rotate the phone to reach the primary button.

hidden.explanation: Blocks a core action for a meaningful share of mobile users, and it is quick to fix.

tickets.title: TLS certificate for the API expires in 9 days
tickets.description: Automatic renewal broke after the DNS move. When the certificate expires, every integration and the mobile clients stop connecting.

hidden.explanation: A total outage with a known date and a tiny fix. It is in the sprint before anything else is discussed.

tickets.title: Let customers invest their idle balance
tickets.description: Everyone I talk to wants their balance to earn something. We should offer an investment product.

visible.impactHint: Everyone I talk to wants this.

hidden.explanation: 'Everyone I talk to' is a sample of the CEO's network. A new regulated product needs demand data first, and none exists.

midSprintEvents.title: Production incident: transfers stuck in 'pending'
midSprintEvents.description: Since 08:40 new transfers are accepted but never leave. Pablo traced it to the payment worker, which crashes on a new bank response code. Customers are calling.

addedTicket.title: Hotfix: payment worker crashes on new bank response code
addedTicket.description: Handle the new response code, restart the worker safely and release the stuck transfers without sending any of them twice.

hidden.explanation: Production is broken for customers right now. Nothing planned before the incident is worth more than ending it.

hidden.guidance: An outage outranks planned work. Pull the hotfix in and take the lowest-value items out to make room: adding it on top of a full sprint only moves the failure to the end of the sprint.
